A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChartCoder, Chart2Code-160k, and Snippet-of-Thought. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ChartCoder benchmark results, architecture and training-data ablations, and an MMC chart-understanding experiment in Section 5 and Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds quantitative chart-quality and code-readability evaluations and another model in the MMC experiment.

M1.justification: Both versions retain SigLIP-384, the two-layer MLP connector, DeepSeek Coder 6.7B, Any Resolution processing, two-stage training, and the same four-step SoT procedure. Removing the introduction's PoT attribution and expanding template descriptions do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: The training corpora, 160k-pair dataset with 27 chart types, and ChartMimic, Plot2Code, ChartX, and MMC tasks remain unchanged. The new quality and readability analyses reuse existing charts and code; extending MMC to another model does not introduce different task requirements.

E2.justification: The main chart-to-code comparator roster is unchanged. However, v2 Table 9 introduces a readability comparison between ChartCoder output, Qwen2-VL-7B output, and human-written ChartMimic code; that reported comparison is absent from v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds GPT-4o evaluation of 8k sampled chart-code pairs using four chart-quality criteria and a separate four-criterion code-readability protocol, documented in Figures 7–8. It also tests InternVL2-8B under the existing MMC image-only/image-plus-code design. Appendix A.1 training settings and the original benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused quantitative checks of synthetic-chart quality against real-world charts and generated-code readability against model and human references. It also extends the code-assisted MMC analysis to a second model. Existing component and backbone ablations, error-type analysis, and case studies are retained; the error plot is relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: v2 Tables 2 and 9 introduce mean and standard-deviation reporting for chart-quality and code-readability scores. v1 has no corresponding dispersion reporting. Neither version documents repeated-training seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new SDs do not establish additional training runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds chart-quality means of 77.32 for generated charts and 78.96 for real-world charts, and readability means of 82.48 for Qwen2-VL-7B, 85.22 for ChartCoder, and 87.66 for human code. Its new InternVL2-8B MMC row reports 0.79 for image-only and 0.82 for image-plus-code. Original benchmark scores, ablation results, and the MiniCPM MMC results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. The added evaluation rubrics are empirical scoring procedures, not new theoretical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: Both abstracts, contribution lists, and conclusions claim the first dedicated chart-to-code MLLM, the 160k-pair diverse dataset, SoT generation, and superior performance over evaluated open-source models. The additional analyses support these retained contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 Section 3.3 adds the interpretation that manual inspection supports training suitability and that generated-chart quality scores are broadly comparable to real-world ChartMimic charts. Existing explanations concerning OCR, resolution, numerical extraction, and language backbones remain unchanged, as do the substantive limitations.

D1.justification: v2 documents manual inspection of about 1k charts and supplies the new scoring prompts and evaluator identity. The abstract changes code availability from promised to available. Section 3.1 newly states '79 template codes,' while Figure 2 still states '89 seed code,' leaving the count inconsistent rather than establishing a changed generation procedure. Existing hardware and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including ChartEdit, academic-chart reproduction, PRISM, and recent multimodal adaptation work, while removing references including Program of Thoughts, ChartQA, ChartInstruct, and MatPlotAgent. These are limited background and attribution revisions; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, shortens background and limitations prose, revises author/contact information, and adds an acknowledgment. The conclusion becomes Section 6 instead of Section 5.5, and a new Output Code Analysis subsection shifts the existing dataset-analysis appendix to A.5. Most narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds two evaluation tables and two boxed scoring-prompt figures, and expands the MMC table to identify both models. The existing error plot moves from the main text to the appendix, and the two appendix case-study figures exchange order. Existing graphical content and the general two-column design remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides explicit quantitative checks of training-chart quality and output-code readability, reproducible scoring prompts, and a second-model MMC result. These modestly strengthen validation and transparency. The gains are limited by reliance on GPT-4o judgments and the newly inconsistent template-count description; the core method and original performance evidence remain unchanged.
